questions.q: For the question 'which accounts have an open opportunity over $50,000,' which pattern fits best?
options: An aggregate query with GROUP BY
A parent-to-child subquery, since you need the Opportunity's own fields
A semi-join — filter Account rows by a related Opportunity fact, without needing Opportunity fields back
A SOSL search, since the question involves free text
questions.explain: Because the question only needs Account rows filtered by a related fact — not the Opportunity's own fields — a semi-join (IN with a subquery) is the cleanest fit.

questions.q: For 'list every open opportunity with its stage and amount, nested under each account,' which pattern fits?
options: A parent-to-child subquery, since the Opportunity fields themselves need to come back nested under each Account
A semi-join, since it's simpler to write
A TYPEOF clause, since opportunities are polymorphic
An anti-join, since you want accounts without opportunities
questions.explain: Needing the actual related records' fields back, nested under their parent, is exactly what a parent-to-child subquery is for — a semi-join would only return matching Account rows, not the Opportunity data.

questions.q: To get total pipeline value and average deal size by stage, limited to stages with more than 3 deals, which two clauses are both required together?
options: OFFSET and LIMIT
WHERE and ORDER BY only
TYPEOF and RETURNING
GROUP BY and HAVING
questions.explain: GROUP BY produces the per-stage summary rows, and HAVING filters those groups down to only stages with more than 3 deals — WHERE alone cannot filter on an aggregated count.

questions.q: In SELECT Name, (SELECT Name, StageName FROM Opportunities ORDER BY Amount DESC) FROM Account, what does the inner ORDER BY affect?
options: The order of the outer Account rows
Only the order of each account's own nested opportunities, independent of how the outer accounts are ordered
Nothing — ORDER BY is not allowed inside a subquery
It sorts both the outer and inner results together as one combined list
questions.explain: A subquery's own ORDER BY only controls the order of that nested result set within each parent row, separate from any ordering on the outer query.

questions.q: What is described as the single most common mistake once a student is past pure SOQL syntax?
options: Using too many WHERE clauses
Forgetting to add a semicolon at the end of a query
Misreading what shape of answer a business question actually wants before writing any SOQL
Always using SELECT * instead of naming fields
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes that picking the right pattern (semi-join vs. subquery vs. GROUP BY/HAVING) based on what the question is really asking matters more than syntax fluency alone.
